title: Why Ice Cream Gives You Brain Freeze (and the Tongue Fix) #science #body
description:
The ice cream is in your mouth, so why does your forehead hurt? Your brain is not freezing. The cold hits the roof of your mouth, and the blood vessels there tighten, then widen again fast. That change is picked up by the trigeminal nerve, which also serves your forehead, so your brain places the pain in the wrong spot (referred pain).

Speed matters: in one randomised trial with 145 pupils, eating ice cream in under 5 seconds gave 27% of them a headache, against 13% for those who took more than 30 seconds.

The fix doctors suggest: press your tongue (or thumb) against the roof of your mouth to warm it back up, or sip something warm. Brain freeze usually passes within seconds to a couple of minutes.
